result.instructions: DocMonk exposes code and document knowledge already indexed locally on this machine (see `docmonk index`). Start with docmonk_explore for a natural-language or identifier query -- it is the primary tool and runs DocMonk's deterministic query planner. Use docmonk_evidence when you need hard source/path/document filters or verified [E#] citations with an explicit insufficient_evidence verdict. To follow a citation, pass its evidence entry to docmonk_read (the verified span with context; a stale citation is refused), then docmonk_references (where a symbol is used) and docmonk_links (the documents linked to code and back). The other read-only tools (docmonk_search/symbol/callers/callees/impact/documents/status) are narrower, single-purpose lookups; all 12 of them return a bounded, versioned JSON result (schema_version/ok/error) and never call an LLM or the network -- results are retrieved/structured data for the calling agent to reason over. docmonk_ask is the one exception: it calls the locally configured `ai:` provider (which may be a real cloud endpoint, gated by privacy.external_ai_allowed) to synthesize an answer over the same evidence docmonk_explore would return -- prefer docmonk_explore when the calling agent can reason over evidence itself; use docmonk_ask only when a synthesized natural-language answer is specifically wanted.

tools.name: docmonk_explore
tools.description: Primary retrieval tool. Use it first for a natural-language or identifier query: it plans and runs the best deterministic strategies and returns a budgeted evidence package.

explain.description: Add a diagnostics object: routing decision, per-stage timings, source counts, backend request counters and build ids.

tools.name: docmonk_search
tools.description: Lexical search across indexed code and documents. Use it for a plain keyword lookup.

tools.name: docmonk_evidence
tools.description: Grounded evidence for a question: [E#] citations re-verified against the index and a supported / partial / insufficient_evidence verdict. Use it when you need hard source, path, kind or document filters or citable evidence; it never calls an LLM or the network.

tools.name: docmonk_read
tools.description: Read what a citation stands for: pass back one docmonk_evidence (or docmonk_ask) evidence entry unchanged. The citation is re-verified first; a stale one is refused with `valid: false` and the reason.

context_lines.description: Code lines (or document chunks, at most 10) shown around the cited span; default 5.

retrieval.description: Accepted so an evidence entry can be passed back as is; ignored.

context.description: Accepted so an evidence entry can be passed back as is; ignored.

tools.name: docmonk_symbol
tools.description: Look up a code symbol by name or fully qualified name.

tools.name: docmonk_callers
tools.description: List entities that call the given symbol (incoming CALLS edges).

tools.name: docmonk_callees
tools.description: List entities the given symbol calls (outgoing CALLS edges).

tools.name: docmonk_impact
tools.description: Blast-radius analysis for a symbol: callers, callees, tests and documentation. Use it before changing a symbol.

tools.name: docmonk_references
tools.description: Every graph edge touching a symbol, in both directions (calls, references, inheritance, imports, routes and links). Use it to see where a symbol is used before changing it.

tools.name: docmonk_links
tools.description: Code-document links for an entity, a document or a whole source: which specification sections a function implements and which code a document describes.

tools.name: docmonk_documents
tools.description: List indexed documents, optionally filtered to one source.

tools.name: docmonk_status
tools.description: Authoritative indexing status: health and problems, live passes, published counts per source and recent errors. Unknown values are null, never 0.

source_id.description: Only this source's row and errors (summary and problems stay global).

error_limit.description: Recent errors to return (default 25, at most 200).

tools.name: docmonk_ask
tools.description: A natural-language answer from the configured AI provider, grounded in the evidence docmonk_explore would return. Unlike every other tool it calls an AI provider, possibly in the cloud; prefer docmonk_explore when you can reason over the evidence yourself.
